question: The owner's second addition, in his words: "What if instead of 'copying', we consume and output 2?" As read: when a first and a second pattern are one part, do births with a parent in each leave two parts the same as the second pattern, each descended from both, with the knots descended from the second pattern only ended, in a way that needs the first pattern (not with the first barred, not in the second alone, not in the first alone) and, for the stricter reading, for every second pattern of a class and not of the others? Arm 1: the six base laws with no taking rule, the two patterns one part at the start. Arm 2: the taking rule that lets parts meet, on ticket A's designs.
inputs: The starts, rosters, base laws, taking rules, renamings and bounds named in the pre-registration and its data files; ticket B's definitions and claim; ticket A's frozen definitions and start file; the definitions of PARTS-MEET-AGAIN-20261124-001 and the shared definitions of RING-IN-BALANCE-20261123-001; the engine of PARTS-MEET-AGAIN-20261124-001A, unchanged, and ticket A's engine for the readings both tickets use.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; for the engine's author, the drafter's scratch prototype and anything it produced beyond what the pre-registration discloses; any change to the fold study's engine or to ticket A's frozen text; any rule added so that a pattern is ended or left twice.
primary_observable: For every registered run: the parts the same as the second pattern's form by descent at every round read; whether the knots descended from the second pattern only have ended, and how; the conditions (a) to (d); whether the first pattern returns; the forms of the parts descended from both for each second pattern; the round after which the roster is the same as a run of one pattern alone; the checks of the settled statements (one law with no taking rule under the first count of fresh distinctions; the roster statement; the marked start roster; renaming); the knot test of every knot under the run's own knot law.
comparators_or_controls: The first pattern barred; the second pattern alone; the first pattern alone; each other member of the class as the second pattern; the control with both patterns of one kind; the four ways the two patterns are one part at the start and the other-member swap; holding for release; renamed starts compared exactly; the two knot laws compared until a closing.
resource_budget: Each run under ten minutes and 8 GB on one process; anything longer through the shared runner with a row in the long-running index. Bounds: 8 rounds, 10 under the cap of three, with the guard of the pre-registration.
first_executable_signal: The gate and the checks of the settled statements; then whether any run with patterns of different kinds has two parts the same as the second pattern descended from both that meet (a) to (d).
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' column; checks, replications and reported readings are marked in words. Each failure of a reading of the claim is reported as by argument or by census, with the clause that failed.
stop_rule: Stop when each reading of the claim has, under each registered law, a case with its three verdicts, or a failure reported as by argument or by census, or the bounded report named in the pre-registration; and every registered run has been made and every prediction has a verdict.
nonclaims: An exploratory study of starts built by hand, to eight or ten rounds. In arm 1 the meeting of the two patterns is supplied by the start, so no case of arm 1 can be called made. A failure by argument under the first ration is a fact about that ration; a failure on the second pattern alone is a fact about the law and that pattern, not about the first pattern, and neither bears on the owner's inkling (assumption A248). The owner's idea is recorded as his and is not evidence. No claim about living things, minds, physics or time.
